key_insight: Align the VAE latent of the reference image with auxiliary high-level semantic/cross-modal features before diffusion, so the diffusion Transformer receives a coherent, shared representation—improving fidelity and controllability over naive concatenation.
problem_solved: Existing reference-to-video (R2V) methods simply append extra semantic or cross-modal features to VAE latents, producing representational mismatch that harms identity preservation, attribute control, and temporal coherence in generated videos.
method: Representation Alignment Module: learn lightweight projection/adapters to map VAE latents and auxiliary semantic/cross-modal features into a shared latent space that preserves spatial detail and high-level semantics.
Alignment objective: train with alignment losses (e.g., contrastive or L2-based consistency terms) so paired reference and semantic features become compatible for generation.

Aligned fusion into diffusion Transformer: feed the aligned, fused representation into the DiT-based video diffusion pipeline (with temporal conditioning/attention) to produce controllable, identity-preserving videos.
impact: Makes reference-to-video generation more reliable and controllable while keeping model complexity low—useful for personalization tasks (virtual try-on, advertising) and for practitioners aiming to integrate multi-modal references into diffusion-based video synthesis.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: show VAE encoder -> alignment module (projections/adapters) merging with semantic features -> diffusion Transformer for video frames.
Before vs. after examples: side-by-side video frame sequences comparing naive concatenation vs. aligned representation results.
Latent-space visualization: t-SNE/UMAP showing how reference latents and semantic features are brought into alignment.
Metric bar chart / table: quantitative comparisons (e.g., FID, CLIP-similarity, identity / temporal consistency) and a small ablation of the alignment loss.
paper_title: RefAlign: Representation Alignment for Reference-to-Video Generation
paper_authors: Lei Wang, YuXin Song, Ge Wu, Haocheng Feng, Hang Zhou
